I MUST DETERMINE WHICH LOCKERS REMAIN OPEN AFTER 100 STUDENTS TOGGLE THEM. EACH
continuation_reasoning:
STUDENT TOGGLES LOCKERS AT INTERVALS EQUAL TO THEIR NUMBER.  
THE KEY IS TO FIGURE OUT HOW MANY TIMES EACH LOCKER IS TOGGLED. A LOCKER IS OPEN IF IT IS TOGGLED AN ODD NUMBER OF TIMES.  
A LOCKER NUMBER N IS TOGGLED BY STUDENTS WHOSE NUMBERS ARE DIVISORS OF N. FOR EXAMPLE, LOCKER 6 IS TOGGLED BY STUDENTS 1, 2, 3, AND 6.  
THE NUMBER OF DIVISORS OF A NUMBER DETERMINES HOW MANY TIMES IT IS TOGGLED. MOST NUMBERS HAVE AN EVEN NUMBER OF DIVISORS, EXCEPT PERFECT SQUARES, WHICH HAVE AN ODD NUMBER.  
THUS, THE LOCKERS THAT REMAIN OPEN ARE THOSE WITH NUMBERS THAT ARE PERFECT SQUARES.  
THE PERFECT SQUARES BETWEEN 1 AND 100 ARE 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, AND 100.  
SO, THESE LOCKERS WILL BE OPEN AT THE END.
